title: Competitive Industries Small Markets: Global Winners report | World Economic Forum
gist: A WEF paper uses five case studies from Indonesia, Peru, Costa Rica, Chile and Viet Nam to argue that small economies can build lasting export competitiveness without subsidy races or trade barriers. Its guiding principles are removing bottlenecks to firm growth, building local capabilities, making a compelling investment case and, critically, keeping public-private collaboration going over time. The case industries run from electric vehicles and agro-exports to aquaculture, precision engineering and IT.

insights.claim: Smaller economies lack the scale and resources to compete in subsidy races or to rely on trade barriers, so they need a different route to globally competitive industries.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: As large economies escalate industrial-policy subsidies, small-market exporters must win on capabilities and investability rather than fiscal firepower, which changes what to look for when assessing their export sectors.
insights.quote: How can smaller economies build globally competitive industries when they lack the scale and resources to compete in subsidy races or rely on trade barriers?
insights.locator: How can smaller economies build globally

insights.claim: Case studies from Indonesia, Peru, Costa Rica, Chile and Viet Nam show businesses and governments building export industries that achieved lasting international competitiveness, in sectors including electric vehicles, agro-exports, aquaculture, precision engineering and IT.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Points to specific emerging-market country and sector pairings that WEF holds up as durable export success stories, which could serve as a starting list for EM export-sector research.

insights.claim: Emerging economies can turn local advantages into internationally competitive industries even in an increasingly fragmented global economy.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Pushes back on the view that geoeconomic fragmentation only hurts small open economies; local advantages plus good policy may still lead to export wins.
insights.quote: how emerging economies can turn local advantages into internationally competitive industries in an increasingly fragmented global economy

insights.claim: The paper's guiding principles for policy-makers and business leaders are overcoming bottlenecks to firm growth, building local capabilities, creating a compelling business case for investment, and sustaining public-private collaboration over time.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Gives a checklist for judging whether a small economy's industrial strategy is investable: look for removed growth bottlenecks, capability building and a clear investment case rather than tariffs or subsidies.
insights.quote: overcoming bottlenecks to firm growth, building local capabilities, creating a compelling business case for investment

insights.claim: Sustained public-private collaboration over time is singled out as the critical factor behind lasting export competitiveness in small markets.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Policy continuity across political cycles becomes a key risk factor when underwriting EM export-sector investments; collaboration that breaks down undermines the model.
insights.quote: critically, sustaining public–private collaboration over time
